text: time--event outcomes, survival::Surv object passed y family = "cox" set. Row names y must match rownames(x). following commands simulate small survival dataset signal first two features construct lambda grid. linear predictor involves first two features , stable selection procedure expected recover . model fitted 40 bootstrap replicates random-permutation artificial features. output lists selected feature names, followed six features largest stability importances. small sample size FDR threshold saturates 1, selection set can empty; planted features g1 g2 instead recovered sorted importances, expected rank top. stability path makes comparison visible: sparse end lambda grid planted features lift away null background, saturated end every curve approaches FDR upper bound (dashed line 1).

title: Advanced stablr Workflows
text: Multinomial outcomes use named factor y. stability matrix one row per feature, importances aggregate across classes. following commands simulate three-class problem weak class signal first feature fit multinomial model. printed vector contains features selected multinomial fit. class signal confined feature m1, feature expected appear among selections.
code: n <- 90 p <- 12 ids <- paste0("s", seq_len(n)) x_multi <- matrix(   rnorm(n * p), nrow = n,   dimnames = list(ids, paste0("m", seq_len(p))) ) y_multi <- factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE), levels = c("A", "B", "C")) names(y_multi) <- ids # Weak class signal from first feature x_multi[y_multi == "B", 1] <- x_multi[y_multi == "B", 1] + 1.5 x_multi[y_multi == "C", 1] <- x_multi[y_multi == "C", 1] - 1.5  lambda_multi <- auto_lambda_grid(x_multi, y_multi, family = "multinomial", n_lambda = 6)  fit_multi <- stabl_fit(   x               = x_multi,   y               = y_multi,   lambda_grid     = lambda_multi,   family          = "multinomial",   n_bootstraps    = 30L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state    = 1L )  get_feature_names(fit_multi) #> character(0)

title: Advanced stablr Workflows
text: several rows belong subject batch, groups vector passed bootstrap resampling keeps whole groups together. prevents leakage across related samples. following commands simulate four repeated measurements per subject, inspect one grouped subsample draw, fit grouped model. call unique(groups[idx]) prints subjects entering one subsample; subject appears either four rows . final line reports number features selected grouped Gaussian fit. fixed hard_threshold = 0.5 used selection set non-empty: ten candidates, default data-driven threshold can legitimately select nothing, make similarity comparisons next section vacuous. Group labels forwarded stabl_multiomic_train_validate() (argument groups_train) stabl_multiomic_cv() (argument groups) outer fold construction. Classification bootstraps redraw subsamples least two observations per class present. slightly biases subsample distribution relative vanilla STABL; deviation deliberate documented, buys class-diverse subsamples.
code: n <- 48 p <- 10 ids <- paste0("s", seq_len(n)) groups <- setNames(rep(paste0("subj", seq_len(12)), each = 4), ids) x_grp <- matrix(   rnorm(n * p), nrow = n,   dimnames = list(ids, paste0("f", seq_len(p))) ) y_grp <- setNames(rnorm(n) + 0.5 * x_grp[, 1], ids)  # Inspect one grouped draw (whole subjects only) idx <- group_bootstrap_indices(y_grp, groups = groups, n_subsamples = 24L, seed = 1L) #> Warning: `seed` is deprecated; use `random_state` instead. unique(groups[idx]) #> [1] "subj9"  "subj4"  "subj8"  "subj1"  "subj3"  "subj10"  lambda_grp <- auto_lambda_grid(x_grp, y_grp, family = "gaussian", n_lambda = 6)  fit_grp <- stabl_fit(   x               = x_grp,   y               = y_grp,   sample_groups   = groups,   lambda_grid     = lambda_grp,   family          = "gaussian",   n_bootstraps    = 25L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   hard_threshold  = 0.5,   random_state    = 3L )  length(get_feature_names(fit_grp)) #> [1] 10

title: Advanced stablr Workflows
text: Selection-stability metrics compare feature lists repeated STABL runs. Jaccard similarity simplest overlap measure, adjusted similarity corrects chance overlap set sizes differ. Two fits different random states compared first, pairwise similarity matrix across four seeds computed afterwards. first two printed values Jaccard adjusted similarity selections seeds 11 22. matrix end gives pairwise Jaccard similarities fits seeds 11 14; -diagonal values close 1 indicate selections robust random state. matrix easier compare heatmap.
code: run_once <- function(seed) {   stabl_fit(     x = x_grp, y = y_grp, sample_groups = groups,     lambda_grid = lambda_grp,     family = "gaussian",     n_bootstraps = 20L,     artificial_type = "random_permutation",     hard_threshold = 0.5,     random_state = seed   ) }  fit_a <- run_once(11L) fit_b <- run_once(22L) sel_a <- get_feature_names(fit_a) sel_b <- get_feature_names(fit_b)  jaccard_similarity(sel_a, sel_b) #> [1] 1 adjusted_similarity(sel_a, sel_b, n_universe = ncol(x_grp)) #> [1] 0  # Pairwise matrix across several seeds fits <- lapply(11:14, run_once) sels <- lapply(fits, get_feature_names) jaccard_similarity_matrix(sels) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    1    1    1 #> [2,]    1    1    1 #> [3,]    1    1    1 #> [4,]    1    1    1 # Keep the full square matrix (remove_diag = FALSE) so both axes carry the # seed labels; as.table() on the diagonal-removed matrix would mislabel the # second axis with row indices instead of seed ids. jm <- jaccard_similarity_matrix(sels, remove_diag = FALSE) dimnames(jm) <- list(seed_a = as.character(11:14), seed_b = as.character(11:14)) jm_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(jm)) names(jm_df) <- c("seed_a", "seed_b", "jaccard") ggplot2::ggplot(jm_df, ggplot2::aes(seed_a, seed_b, fill = jaccard)) +   ggplot2::geom_tile() +   ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(     label = sprintf("%.2f", jaccard)   )) +   ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey90") +   ggplot2::labs(x = "random_state", y = "random_state",                 title = "Selection overlap across repeated fits") +   ggplot2::theme_minimal()

Evidence status (simulation-, predeclared gates, benchmarks/iv_summary.md): effect-direction recovery 1.00; null validated AUROC centred chance (median 0.473); leaky full-data selection directionally optimistic nested validation (+0.015 mean AUROC); one-feature folds produce non-degenerate probabilities. One predeclared criterion met: correlated substitutes always assigned single correlation group co-selected, FDP+ selection retains members correlated block 60% runs — expect complete co-selection redundant features. Multiclass ordinal graduation remain reserved (WS-9 ordinal graduation met).

title: stablr
text: stablr R-native without Python runtime. core STABL method parity-tested Python STABL implementation (Hédou et al. 2024); cross-language solver validation uses ranking/support contracts claim bit-identical coefficients. cooperative-learning backend compiled C++17 (vendored multiview engine), learners come glmnet ecosystem: lasso, elastic net, adaptive lasso, optional sparse group lasso, gaussian, binomial, multinomial, Cox outcomes backend supports family. random-forest learner (ranger) ordinal-regression learner (ordinalNet) also available base learners. interface two-tier. stabl() runs STABL statistically safe defaults — model-X knockoff artificial features, FDP+ calibration, strict fallback, automatic lambda grid — prints plain-language answer: stabl_fit() exposes every argument — lambda grids, bootstrap design, thresholds, learner adapters, sample grouping — every accessor workflow applies objects. See ?stabl_fit vignettes. Everything beyond core STABL labelled extension. Cooperative fusion (Ding et al. 2022) ships vendored multiview engine gaussian binomial families (Cox deferred). random-forest learner calibrated scoped settings: linear nonlinear gaussian problems dozen predictors (see ?make_ranger_adapter). ordinal learner experimental pending calibration study (see ?make_ordinal_adapter). environment-stability workflow aggregates per-environment selections minimum frequency; calibrated small feature panels (see ?stabl_environment_stability). Interpretation limits part contract. fitted threshold first minimizer observed FDP+ curve; plotted fdr_target visual reference, fitting target, neither universal false-discovery guarantee. Knockoff modes fail closed 3,000 predictors globally valid chunked construction established; random-permutation controls remain available larger dimensions.
code: library(stablr) fit <- stabl(df, y = "response", n_bootstraps = 1000L, random_state = 42L) fit                    # plain-language answer feature_names(fit)     # the selected features plot(fit)              # stability paths + FDP+ curve

text: Computes chance-corrected similarity two feature sets.  Unlike jaccard_similarity(), adjusted measure accounts expected random overlap given sizes sets total feature universe, systematically penalise methods select many features.

title: Adjusted Similarity Between Two Feature Sets — adjusted_similarity
text: set1 Character integer vector selected feature identifiers. set2 Character integer vector selected feature identifiers. n_universe Integer; total number candidate features universe (.e. number columns original predictor matrix). list1 Deprecated; use set1 instead.  supplied name, deprecation warning emitted value used set1 latter NULL.  removed future release. list2 Deprecated; use set2 instead.  supplied name, deprecation warning emitted value used set2 latter NULL.  removed future release. nb_total_elements Deprecated; use n_universe instead.  supplied name, deprecation warning emitted value used n_universe latter NULL.  removed future release.

title: Adjusted Similarity Between Two Feature Sets — adjusted_similarity
text: Numeric scalar \((-1, 1]\).  Values 0 indicate overlap expected chance; 1 means perfect agreement; negative values indicate less overlap chance.

title: Adjusted Similarity Between Two Feature Sets — adjusted_similarity
text: formula analogous Cohen's kappa sets: $$S_{\text{adj}}(, B) =   \frac{r - \mathbb{E}[r]}{\min(k_1, k_2) - \max(0, k_1 + k_2 - d)}$$ \(r = |\cap B|\), \(k_i = |A_i|\), \(d =\) n_universe, \(\mathbb{E}[r] = k_1 k_2 / d\). Returns 0 either set empty equals full universe (edge cases correction denominator zero).

title: Adjusted Similarity Between Two Feature Sets — adjusted_similarity
code: # 10-feature universe; sets A and B share 2 out of 3 features each adjusted_similarity(c("f1","f2","f3"), c("f2","f3","f4"), n_universe = 10L) #> [1] 0.3666667 adjusted_similarity(c("f1","f2"),      c("f1","f2"),      n_universe = 10L) # 0.8 #> [1] 0.8 adjusted_similarity(character(0),      c("f1"),           n_universe = 10L) # 0 #> [1] 0

what: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: Sweeps grid stability-score thresholds computes FDP+ estimate one, identifies threshold minimises .  direct port Stabl._compute_FDPplus() Python STABL library.

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
code: compute_fdp_plus(   stabl_scores,   stabl_scores_artificial,   artificial_proportion,   fdr_threshold_range = seq(0, 0.99, by = 0.01) )

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: stabl_scores Numeric matrix (features \(\times\) lambdas) stability scores real features. stabl_scores_artificial Numeric matrix (artificial features \(\times\) lambdas) stability scores injected noise features. artificial_proportion Positive numeric scalar; fraction artificial features relative real features (used \(\pi\)). fdr_threshold_range Numeric vector threshold values sweep. Default: seq(0, 0.99, = 0.01), matching Python STABL's np.arange(0., 1., .01).

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: Named list: FDRs Numeric vector FDP+ estimates, one per threshold. min_fdr Minimum FDP+ achieved across threshold range. fdr_min_threshold Threshold value achieving min_fdr, capped 1. fdrs_table Numeric matrix (lambdas \(\times\) thresholds) per-lambda FDP+ values.

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
text: FDP+ threshold \(\tau\) estimated : $$\widehat{\text{FDP}}(\tau) =   \frac{(1/\pi) \cdot |\{j : \hat{q}_j^{\text{art}} > \tau\}| + 1}        {\max(1,\, |\{j : \hat{q}_j > \tau\}|)}$$ \(\pi\) artificial_proportion, \(\hat{q}_j\) maximum--lambda stability scores real feature \(j\), \(\hat{q}_j^{\text{art}}\) scores artificial feature \(j\).

title: Compute FDP+ (False Discovery Proportion Upper Bound) — compute_fdp_plus
code: # Small synthetic stability-score matrices (3 real + 3 artificial features, # 2 lambda values) scores_real <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.6, 0.1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.05), nrow = 3) scores_art  <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.15, 0.25, 0.1), nrow = 3) result <- compute_fdp_plus(scores_real, scores_art,                            artificial_proportion = 1.0) result$min_fdr           # minimum FDP+ estimate #> [1] 0.5 result$fdr_min_threshold # threshold that achieves it #> [1] 0.3

text: y Outcome vector length groups. groups Vector group identifiers (length y).  Values may type supports unique() equality comparison. n_subsamples Positive integer; target number rows subsample.  actual count may differ slightly due whole-group granularity (whole groups always preserved; realised count smallest group-aligned value >= n_subsamples). replace Logical; may group sampled ? Default FALSE. stratify Logical; TRUE, sample whole groups within outcome strata realised subsample retains class representation group structure permits .  group must map exactly one outcome class.  Whole groups still preserved, realised counts can exceed per-class targets.  Default FALSE. strata Optional categorical stratification design.  Provide vector one stratification factor, data.frame/matrix/list joint design across multiple factors.  group must map exactly one realised stratum. random_state Optional integer; seed used draw.  function clobber caller's global RNG state: previous .Random.seed restored exit (via withr::local_seed()). seed Deprecated; use random_state instead.  supplied, deprecation warning emitted value used random_state latter NULL.  removed future release.

title: Group-Aware Bootstrap Sampler Indices — group_bootstrap_indices
text: group-level sampling prevents leakage: individual rows subject appear bootstrap subsample complement, stability score becomes inflated learner can partially memorise subject-level patterns.  sampling complete groups, subsample "holdout" subject-disjoint, preserving independence assumption underlying STABL's FDP+ diagnostic assumptions. groups sampled: Groups drawn one time (without replacement default) running tally included rows reaches exceeds n_subsamples.  Whole groups always kept intact: last added group causes count exceed n_subsamples, surplus rows trimmed.  guarantees strongest leakage prevention (subsample complement always group-disjoint), cost slightly variable subsample size.  replace = TRUE group may drawn multiple times (useful groups). Degenerate bootstrap guard: sample_bootstrap_indices(), final subsample contains one unique class function retries class-diverse sample obtained.

code: set.seed(42) n <- 50L p <- 10L x <- matrix(   rnorm(n * p),   nrow = n,   dimnames = list(paste0("s", seq_len(n)), paste0("f", seq_len(p))) ) y <- setNames(0.8 * x[, 1] - 0.5 * x[, 2] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), rownames(x)) lambda_grid <- data.frame(lambda = seq(0.02, 0.30, length.out = 4L))  # Default lasso path fit_lasso <- stabl_fit(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   n_bootstraps = 6L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state = 1L ) get_feature_names(fit_lasso) #> [1] "f1" "f2"  # Adaptive lasso path fit_adaptive <- stabl_fit(   x = x,   y = y,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   base_learner = "adaptive_lasso",   adaptive_gamma = 1.0,   adaptive_epsilon = 1e-6,   n_bootstraps = 6L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state = 2L ) get_importances(fit_adaptive) #>        f1        f2        f3        f4        f5        f6        f7        f8  #> 1.0000000 1.0000000 0.5000000 0.8333333 0.8333333 0.3333333 0.6666667 0.6666667  #>        f9       f10  #> 0.3333333 0.5000000   # Sparse-group lasso path (optional dependency) if (requireNamespace("sparsegl", quietly = TRUE)) {   feature_groups <- rep(seq_len(5L), each = 2L)   fit_sgl <- stabl_fit(     x = x,     y = y,     lambda_grid = lambda_grid,     base_learner = "sparse_group_lasso",     feature_groups = feature_groups,     n_bootstraps = 5L,     artificial_type = "random_permutation",     random_state = 3L   )   get_support(fit_sgl) } #>    f1    f2    f3    f4    f5    f6    f7    f8    f9   f10  #>  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE   # Multinomial path with three classes y_multi <- setNames(   factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE)),   rownames(x) ) fit_multi <- suppressWarnings(stabl_fit(   x = x,   y = y_multi,   lambda_grid = lambda_grid,   family = "multinomial",   n_bootstraps = 5L,   artificial_type = "random_permutation",   random_state = 4L )) get_feature_names(fit_multi) #> [1] "f1" "f2" "f3" "f4" "f5" "f6" "f8" "f9"

title: stablr 0.3.0.9000 (development)
text: nine vignettes audited current API re-rendered. Replaced 25 deprecated get_feature_names_out() calls get_feature_names(), jaccard_matrix() jaccard_similarity_matrix(), adjusted_similarity(nb_total_elements=) n_universe=, deprecated groups= arguments stabl_fit() sample_groups= (advanced, environments). Corrected stabl_multiomic_train_validate() group argument groups_train (multiomic, cooperative) stale groups note environments vignette. Added seven figure chunks key conclusions visually supported: environment-wise minimum-score heatmap (environments), Cox stability path, Jaccard similarity heatmap interpretation scatter (advanced), late-fusion prediction scatter (multiomic), cooperative rho surface (cooperative), FDR+ regularisation curve (intro). Advanced vignette: grouped-bootstrap reproducibility examples now pass hard_threshold = 0.5 demonstration selects non-empty set p = 10 (default data-driven threshold legitimately selects nothing , made Jaccard comparison vacuous); Cox example text now states FDR threshold saturates 1, selection set empty planted features recovered importances ranking sparse end stability path. Multiomic vignette: late-fusion scatter accompanied honest note compact build settings (10 bootstraps, 6-lambda grids) demonstrate workflow shape, competitive prediction. Intro vignette: section 7.3 benchmark table replaced current learner-benchmark calibration ratios (benchmarks/learner_comparison/), next-steps pointers added getting-started vignette sPLS-DA / random-forest material. Getting-started vignette: corrected knockoff_equi “” table cell – decoys conservative tree learners, measured calibration learner- regime-dependent (see pairing table vignette("stablr-intro")). sPLS-DA coverage extended: new section advanced vignette (multinomial data via binomial adapter), topic-table row, bullet TCGA learner notes, adapter pointer cooperative DIABLO paragraph.

title: stablr 0.3.0.9000 (development)
text: New experimental base learner base_learner = "splsda": sparse PLS discriminant analysis via mixOmics binary classification (family = "binomial" ). STABL lambda grid sweeps sPLS-DA’s per-component keepX; feature counts selected retained component loading exceeds splsda_ncomp-independent magnitude 1e-10. New exports: make_splsda_adapter() (standalone adapter factory, mirroring make_glmnet_adapter()) auto_splsda_keepx_grid() (geometric keepX grid used lambda_grid = "auto"), plus stabl_fit(splsda_ncomp = 2L) argument. Empirical calibration multi-cohort benchmark (benchmarks/mint_comparison/): sPLS-DA + random permutation best-calibrated configuration (FDP/FDP+ ratio 1.01); knockoff pairings validated per dataset.

title: stablr 0.3.0
text: Interpretation/validated-workflow benchmark committed (IV, 110 runs, predeclared gates): effect-direction recovery 1.00, null validated AUROC centred chance (median 0.473), leaky full-data selection directionally optimistic nested (+0.015 mean AUROC), one-feature folds non-degenerate. Redundancy co-selection gate met (0.60): correlated substitutes always grouped co-selected (10/10), FDP+ selection prunes members 4/10 seeds. Adverse result committed (benchmarks/iv_summary.md; Gate B report docs/plans/). Ordinal regression learner (base_learner = "ordinal", ordinalNet proportional-odds): simulated calibration (10 seeds x 2 designs) gives knockoff_equi mean FDP+ 0.00 (nominal 0.1) mean TPR 0.37 – strongly conservative; graduation bar (FDP+ <= 0.15, TPR >= 0.8) met, learner stays experimental (benchmarks/ws9_summary.md). (simulation evidence; summaries benchmarks/) Random-forest adapter graduated within measured scope (WS-2, 60 runs): rf + knockoff_equi meets predeclared criterion (mean FDP <= 0.15, TPR >= 0.8) linear low-dimensional nonlinear designs; met p = 50 strong correlation binary outcomes.
